skill1: Unchanging Heart: Gain Indomitability for 9 sec. Activates 1 time(s) during battle.
Equally shares HP recovery for 5 sec.
skill2: immune to stack count increase or decrease effects continuously. This effect cannot be removed.

caveats: ⚑ EVERY numeric cadence/economy assumption below is UNMEASURED. The kit text supplies all magnitudes; the TRIGGERS for two damage lines and the swap shot economy are inferred.

⚑ 'Memory Absorption takes effect' is modeled as the every-3s stack tick (skill2 line 1). If the stack tick STOPS 'taking effect' once the pool is capped at 30 (t≈90s), then skill1's ally core/ATK buffs and the self-heal go DEAD after ~90s — a large swing. Modeled here as continuing to fire for the whole fight.

⚑ The 380.46% 'stage target' line carries NO activation clause. Modeled as a rider on the SAME trigger as the preceding 150% Memory-Incineration full-charge line (i.e. the full charge deals 150% to all enemies plus 380.46% extra to the stage target). Alternative reading: an independent interval-triggered hit. This choice is worth 5x the 150% line and must be pinned from popups before trusting the burst-window total.

⚑ 'attacking with Full Charge while in Memory Incineration' is modeled as shotFired + swapGate:'swapped' — i.e. EVERY swapped shot is assumed to be a full charge (1.8s fixed charge time). If the engine can fire partial charges while swapped, this over-counts the riders.
⚑ flatDamage crit:true on both damage lines follows the RIDERCRIT prior (riders crit at the caster's sheet rate); neither is core-tagged (no 'core strike damage' wording).
⚑ noFb is deliberately NOT set anywhere — FB is taken by timing (default ON). The burst-cast damage lands pre-FB by timing, so no explicit exemption is authored.

⚑ The stage-1/2/3 thresholds (2/10/30 stacks) are modeled with a named resource + resourceGate rather than `escalating` (which is activation-count-, not threshold-, keyed). The resource-gain effect is ordered FIRST in the slot so the gates read the post-gain pool; if the engine evaluates gates before the same-frame gain, every stage arrives one tick (3s) late — immaterial at fight scale.
Continuous (no-durationSec) self-buffs carry maxStacks:1 so the every-3s re-application refreshes rather than accumulating.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Blind second read of nayuta (SMG/Wind/Supporter/Burst II) from kit prose only. Structure: skill2 is a 3s-tick stack engine (Memory Absorption, +1.4% Hit Rate/stack to 30 = +42% at cap, reached t≈90s) that both self-buffs in three stack-gated stages (ATK 15.2% at ≥2, Attack Damage 20.27% at ≥10, core damage 21.05% at ≥30) and drives skill1's ally package (core damage 25.15% + casterAtk 30.16% for 5s, re-applied every 3s = effectively permanent uptime) plus a 25%-Max-HP self-heal that fires the recovery trigger every 3s (tandem: heal-synergy consumers). Burst is a 15s team Attack Damage 35.45%, a 645.33% burst-skill hit, and a 10s Memory Incineration weapon swap (275.18%/shot, 1.8s fixed charge, 250% full-charge mult, unlimited ammo) that ALSO arms skill1's full-charge riders (150% + 380.46%). The two riders and the swap shot economy are the whole burst-window damage story and are the least-constrained part of this parse.

flags.field: skill1[0].trigger / skill1[1].trigger / skill2[*].trigger — 'Memory Absorption takes effect' cadence + cap behaviour
flags.estimate: interval 3s, first fire t=3s, continues firing for the whole fight even at the 30-stack cap
flags.reasoning: The kit names the stack tick as 'every 3 sec' but never says whether the tick still 'takes effect' once Memory Absorption is capped at 30 and 'immune to stack count increase' effects. If it stops, skill1's ally core/ATK buffs and the self-heal DIE at t≈90s — a very large swing on a 180s fight. Interval first-fire phase (t=sec vs t=0) is also a repo convention, not kit text.
flags.recipe: Record a solo/graded run past 120s and watch the team's buff icons (or a popup-value step) at the 90s mark: if the ally ATK/core buff icons persist past t≈95s the modeled reading is right; if they lapse, re-key skill1's blocks to a capped stack window. Cross-check first-fire by timestamping the FIRST appearance of the ally buff icon (t≈0 vs t≈3).

flags.estimate: same trigger as the 150% line (shotFired while swapped) → ~5 procs per burst window
flags.reasoning: The line has its own ■ header with a CONDITION clause ('if the enemy is the stage target') but NO activation clause, which the methodology maps to `interval` by default. Structurally it reads as the single-target half of the preceding Memory-Incineration full-charge hit (150% to all enemies + 380.46% extra to the stage target) — a common NIKKE pattern. The alternative (an independent always-on interval hit) would fire ~60x per fight instead of ~5x per burst and would dominate her damage. This is the single largest uncertainty in the parse.
flags.recipe: Record a fight and count 380.46%-magnitude popups: if they appear ONLY during the 10s Memory Incineration window and 1:1 with the 150% popups, the rider reading holds; if they appear on a fixed clock outside the burst window, re-key to interval and read the period off the popup timestamps.

flags.field: burst[2].effects[0] — weaponSwap shot economy (pullsPerSec / weapon class / shots per window)
flags.estimate: ~5 full charges in the 10s window (10 / 1.8s charge), each at 275.18% × 250% = 687.95% of final ATK; base SMG class retained for range banding
flags.reasoning: Kit-silent on the swap weapon's class and on cast/recovery frames between charges, and the datamined cadence fields are the known-unreliable ones. 10/1.8 = 5.55 charges is the optimistic ceiling; any per-shot recovery frame drops it to 5, and a mid-window burst-banner freeze could drop it to 4. Setting `weapon` wrongly would shift the range band, so it is deliberately left unset.
flags.recipe: Frame-count the Memory Incineration window in a recording: count charge-shot popups between the swap banner and its expiry, and time the gap between consecutive popups to get the true charge+recovery period. Set pullsPerSec (and `weapon` if the swap sprite is clearly not an SMG) from that.

flags.estimate: 42% Hit Rate at cap (30 × 1.4%), converted by the engine's hrCoreMult path
flags.reasoning: Hit Rate → core-hit rate is a derived engine relationship (⚑ per the ALWAYS-⚑ taxonomy), never stated in kit text. A +42% Hit Rate is a very large lift and it lands on a Supporter whose whole team is also carrying her +25.15%/+21.05% core-damage buffs, so an error here compounds across the comp.
flags.recipe: Run the existing accuracy-geometry / HRCORE tooling (docs/data/sg-calc, the HRCORE gate) at 0 vs 42 Hit Rate for an SMG and compare the predicted core fraction against a popup CORE-HIT count from a recorded run. The geometry is the ground-truth instrument here, not damage-back-derivation.

flags.field: skill2 stack trajectory / stage-gate arrival times
flags.estimate: stack N at t = 3N sec → stage 1 at t≈6s, stage 2 at t≈30s, stage 3 at t≈90s; time-average over a 180s fight ≈ 100% stage1, ~83% stage2, ~50% stage3
flags.reasoning: DERIVED from stated values (every 3s, +1 stack, cap 30) rather than guessed — the kit gives start, rate, and cap, so no haircut estimate is needed. But it assumes exactly one stack per tick and that the tick starts at battle start; if the first tick is t=0 every arrival shifts 3s earlier.
flags.recipe: Read the Memory Absorption stack counter off a recording at t=30 and t=90 (should read 10 and 30). If the counter runs faster, the tick is not a clean 3s or grants >1 stack.

flags.field: skill1[2]/skill1[3].swapGate + trigger — 'attacking with Full Charge' modeled as every swapped shot
flags.estimate: 1 rider proc per swapped shot (~5 per burst)
flags.reasoning: The riders require a FULL charge specifically. Because Memory Incineration fixes charge time at 1.8s, every deliberate shot in the window should be a full charge — but if the engine fires uncharged/partial shots while swapped, shotFired over-counts the riders, and the 380.46% line makes that error expensive.
flags.recipe: Same recording as the swap-economy flag: confirm the 150% popup count equals the charge-shot count in the window. If the engine can emit non-full-charge swapped shots, add a charge-specific gate or move the riders onto the swap's own full-charge path.

flags.field: skill1[2]/skill1[3]/burst[1] — flatDamage crit:true, core absent, noFb unset
flags.estimate: all three hits crit at the caster's sheet rate, none receive core, all take FB by timing
flags.reasoning: Follows the standing priors (RIDERCRIT makes flat riders crit-eligible; no 'core strike damage' wording anywhere in the kit so no core; per-kit noFb is measured-only and defaults OFF). None of the three is measured for this unit.
flags.recipe: Popup colour read: orange/crit-icon popups at the 150%/380.46%/645.33% magnitudes confirm crit eligibility; a red 'CORE HIT' at those magnitudes would refute the no-core call. Compare in-FB vs out-of-FB popup magnitudes at the same buff state to confirm the +50% FB major applies.
